To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the left anterior negativity (Lan) and the parietal P600 (P600) are both involved in the processing and integration of filler gap dependencies in German.

(1) topicalization structures elicit a LAN relative to gap free control sentences, (2) wh questions elicit a P600 relative to topicalization sentences, and (3) wh questions elicits an LAN relative to gap control sentences.
topicalization and wh questions elicit a LAN and a P600, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of working memory in the processing of complex syntactic dependencies, as well as the role of memory load and integration difficulty in the processing of different types of filler-gap dependencies.
the role of working memory and memory integration in sentence processing.
the question of whether there is a single, general mechanism for processing all types of filler gap dependencies, or whether different mechanisms are involved.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the processing of filler gaps in topicalization constructions is easier than in wh questions.
the LAN is not a memory related process but a general process involved in the processing syntactic dependencies.
the processing of topicalization and WH questions is different in that the topicalization construction requires less integration effort than the WH question.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
topicalization and wh constructions differ in their processing costs, with topicalization being less demanding than wh constructions.
there are two separable parsing processes involved in the processing syntactic dependency.
the processing of syntactically complex sentences is a highly interactive process that involves both memory and integration processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
topicalization structures and wh questions are processed differently, and that these differences are not restricted to a late stage in sentence processing.
the processing of filler gaps in German is sensitive to both the syntactic and the semantic properties of the filler and the gap.

the ERP signature of the filler gap dependencies can be modulated by the type of dependency involved, and that these differences in ERP responses are likely to reflect differences in the processing demands of these different types of filler-gap dependency.
